substantiveFindings: Owner pass over the complete chapter: all 373 Chinese units with both English fields, all 3 retained people, 6 surface rows, 29 claims, 266 preflight candidates (259 dispositioned in 10 groups; the remaining 7 are the name/title surfaces consumed by the three people's mentions), the 14 date-audit findings and the 10 accepted editorial repairs.

No missing person or mention. The chapter is a ritual-procedure treatise (guest rites, military rites, archery, eclipse drumming, the great nuo exorcism); every other agent is an unnamed office-holder or role in a prescriptive template (侍中, 中書令, 兵部尚書, 千牛將軍, 太祝, 方相氏, 唱帥, the generic 皇帝, the template 蕃主/某主). The twelve spirits of s0366 (甲作, 胇胃, 雄伯, 騰簡, 攬諸, 伯奇, 彊梁, 祖明, 委隨, 錯斷, 窮奇, 騰根) are exorcistic deities in a chant, not persons; 伯奇 here is the dream-eating spirit, not the Zhou figure Yin Boqi.

No identity, relationship or event-subject defect. Dezong's refusal (s0345), Dong Jin's memorial (s0346), the non-reply (s0347) and the abandonment of the rite (s0348) form one dated episode; the claims assign each action to the correct actor.

Chronology: the 14 research holds are generic 'not yet independently verified' holds, not source contradictions. The only explicit date is 貞元三年八月 (s0345); the owner's proposed treatment for each hold is recorded in holdDispositionProposals. No year is invented, removed or narrowed.

Nine definite English errors found in units with no person mention and no date evidence; complete before/after replacements are in definiteTranslationRepairs (16 field edits). 太常卿 'Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple' was considered and left unchanged: it is an existing corpus rendering (23 extraction occurrences alongside 99 of 'Chief Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices'), it is mirrored in claim c0010/c0025 labels, and changing it is a corpus-convention decision rather than a definite chapter-local error.

definiteTranslationRepairs.before: He then proclaims the command; again twice bows with forehead to the ground.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: The attendant within the palace then proclaims the command; the barbarian lord again twice bows with forehead to the ground.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: 乃宣制 is performed by the 侍中 who descended in s0047 with 「有制」; the bowing 又再拜稽首 is the foreign lord's. The English has no subject for the bow and leaves 'He' ambiguous, so it can be read as the lord proclaiming. Explicit subjects restore the source's actors.

definiteTranslationRepairs.before: He then proclaims the command; the foreign lord again kowtows twice.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: The palace attendant then proclaims the command; the foreign lord again kowtows twice.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: Same as the literal field: 宣制 belongs to the 侍中 of s0047, not to the foreign lord who has just bowed in s0048.

definiteTranslationRepairs.before: The barbarian lord twice bows; he then proclaims the command.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: The barbarian lord twice bows; the attendant within the palace then proclaims the command.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: In s0067 the 侍中 descends and announces 「有制」; 乃宣制 in s0068 is his proclamation. 'he then proclaims' grammatically makes the barbarian lord the proclaimer, an attribution error.

definiteTranslationRepairs.before: The foreign lord bows twice; he then proclaims the command.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: The foreign lord bows twice; the palace attendant then proclaims the command.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: Same attribution error as the literal field: the proclaimer is the 侍中 of s0067, not the foreign lord.

definiteTranslationRepairs.before: He orders six temple stewards to lead exorcists in separately through the Changle Gate and Yongan Gate to the left and right upper pavilions, beating drums and clamoring as they advance.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: He goes out and orders six eunuch stewards (sibo) to lead exorcists in separately through the Changle Gate and Yongan Gate to the left and right upper pavilions, beating drums and clamoring as they advance.

definiteTranslationRepairs.zh: 祝史持版於座右，跪讀祝文曰：「維某年歲次月朔日，天子遣太祝臣姓名昭告于太陰之神。」
definiteTranslationRepairs.before: The invoker-clerk holds the placard at the mat's right side, kneels and reads the prayer: "In such-and-such a year, on such-and-such a day of the first month, the Son of Heaven dispatches Grand Invoker, your subject so-and-so, to announce to the spirit of the Great Yin."
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: The invoker-clerk holds the placard at the mat's right side, kneels and reads the prayer: "In such-and-such a year, with the year-star at such-and-such, in such-and-such a month whose new-moon day is such-and-such, on such-and-such a day, the Son of Heaven dispatches Grand Invoker, your subject so-and-so, to announce to the spirit of the Great Yin."
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: 維某年歲次月朔日 is the standard blank prayer dating formula (year, 歲次 year-star position, month, 朔 new-moon day, day); it does not mean 'the first month'. The current wording invents a 正月 date and drops 歲次 and 朔.

evidence.quote: 貞元三年八月，日有食之，有司將伐鼓，德宗不許。

holdDispositionProposals.ownerFinding: Explicit regnal date 貞元三年八月 owned by the eclipse episode in which Dezong personally refused the drumming. Zhenyuan is Tang Dezong's era (Zhenyuan 1 = AD 785), so year 3 = AD 787; the eighth lunar month of that year lies wholly within AD 787, so year precision is safe. Event owner is Dezong (德宗不許).
holdDispositionProposals.proposedTreatment: approve-unchanged (AD 787, precision year). The host reign table data/people/chronology/reigns.json has no Tang 貞元 entry, so the host should attach its reusable calendar witness for Zhenyuan 1 = 785 rather than commission research.

holdDispositionProposals.ownerFinding: 不報 directly answers Dong Jin's memorial in s0346 within the same dated episode; the omitted subject is the emperor addressed, Dezong. The date is contextual from s0345.
holdDispositionProposals.proposedTreatment: approve-unchanged; the dateContext is inherited from the explicitly dated episode

holdDispositionProposals.ownerFinding: 由是 makes the abandonment of the rite a consequence of the 787 episode; the claim is already marked strongly-inferred and attaches the episode date as context, not as a precise date of abolition.
